subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 5-month-old boy is brought for irritability, poor feeding, and stiffness of the limbs; he has lost the ability to grasp objects. Examination shows increased muscle tone and hyperreflexia, and funduscopy reveals optic nerve atrophy. Nerve biopsy shows multinucleated globoid cells.
question: Deficiency of which of the following enzymes is most likely responsible?
explanation_correct: Irritability, spasticity, developmental regression, optic atrophy, and multinucleated globoid cells in white matter indicate Krabbe disease. Galactocerebrosidase deficiency allows galactocerebroside and psychosine to accumulate and destroy oligodendrocytes and myelin. The disorder is autosomal recessive and usually presents in infancy.

explanation_incorrect.A: Hexosaminidase A deficiency causes Tay-Sachs disease with neuronal GM2 ganglioside accumulation and a cherry-red spot, not globoid cells.
explanation_incorrect.B: Sphingomyelinase deficiency causes Niemann-Pick disease with hepatosplenomegaly and a cherry-red spot.
explanation_incorrect.C: Arylsulfatase A deficiency causes metachromatic leukodystrophy with metachromatic granules, not globoid cells.
explanation_incorrect.D: Glucocerebrosidase deficiency causes Gaucher disease with Gaucher cells and bone disease.

educationalObjective: Krabbe disease is caused by galactocerebrosidase deficiency, with galactocerebroside and psychosine accumulation destroying oligodendrocytes and producing globoid cells.
